chunks: Sa'd ibn 'Abdillah from Musa ibn al-Hasan and al-Hasan ibn 'Ali from Ahmad ibn Hilal from Umayyah ibn 'Ali from al-Husayn ibn 'Uthman said:

I saw Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) praying the two obligatory rak'ahs opposite the Maqam (Station of Abraham), close to the shadows due to the multitude of people. As for the time of the two rak'ahs of Tawaf, it is when one finishes from the Tawaf, provided it is not the time of an obligatory prayer, whether that is after the morning prayer or after the afternoon prayer. And that which indicates this is what he narrated:

key_terms.الْمَقَامُ: The Station of Abraham in the Kaaba
key_terms.رَكْعَتَا الطَّوَافِ: The two rak'ahs of prayer performed after circumambulation

ai.seo_question: When should the two rak'ahs of Tawaf prayer be performed in relation to the obligatory prayers?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the jurisprudential ruling that the two rak'ahs of Tawaf are performed immediately after circumambulation, provided they do not overlap with the time of a mandatory prayer. The inclusion of the Imam’s practice near the Maqam Ibrahim highlights the practical adaptation of ritual space during peak pilgrimage times, reinforcing the flexibility within Shia fiqh regarding the timing of supererogatory acts in the Holy Sanctuary.
